'''Corman Jeihn''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] from [[Calabosh-2]] where he served for a time as a security guard for the weapons manufacturing company [[Caliban (manufacturer)/Legends|Caliban]]. When the company was [[Imperialization/Legends|nationalized]] by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] for supporting the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], Jeihn left Caliban and moved to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]], where he became a member of the [[Bespin Wing Guard/Legends|Bespin Wing Guard]]. In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], just prior to the [[Occupation of Bespin]], Jeihn was present with [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], [[Lobot/Legends|Lobot]], and several of his fellow Wing Guardsmen to greet a group of Rebels when they arrived on the floating [[Mining/Legends|mining]] colony of [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]]. After the Rebels were captured by forces of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], Jeihn, Lobot and several other Wing Guardsmen proceeded to ambush an Imperial unit led by [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Sheckil/Legends|Sheckil]] and free three of the Rebels on Calrissian's orders.

==Biography==
Born on [[Calabosh-2]], the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] Corman Jeihn took work on his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] as security for the [[Caliban (manufacturer)/Legends|Caliban]] arms-manufacturing company. He remained with the company<ref name="SWI" /> until it was discovered by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] that they had been selling weapons to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]],<ref name="A&EG">''[[Arms & Equipment Guide]]''</ref> at which point Caliban was nationalised and its assets absorbed by [[Imperial Munitions/Legends|Imperial Munitions]], and Jeihn left Calabosh-2. He traveled to the planet [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]], where he found work in the [[Bespin Wing Guard/Legends|Bespin Wing Guard]], policing [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]].<ref name="SWI" /> In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> the Empire once again impacted on his life however, when an Imperial force lead by the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] arrived on Cloud City in order to capture a group of Rebels headed to Bespin. The [[Baron Administrator/Legends|Baron Administrator]] of the [[City/Legends|city]], [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], struck a deal with Vader in which he promised to help the Imperials capture the Rebels as long as Cloud City was left free of Imperial control.<ref name="ESB" /> Jeihn, along with five other Wing Guards;<ref name="ESB" /> [[Bialar Selis]], [[Fin Mak'lath]], [[Fantes Mer'darro]], [[Allen Neff]] and [[Helder Spinoza/Legends|Helder Spinoza]],<ref name="SWI" /> accompanied Calrissian and his Chief administrative aide [[Lobot/Legends|Lobot]] to [[Platform 327/Legends|Platform 327]] in Cloud City to greet the Rebels when they arrived. He and the five other guardsmen stood silently as Calrissian met with his old friends [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], along with their new companions [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] and [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], none of whom knew that a trap awaited them within the city.<ref name="ESB" />

[[File:FashionableFelonFindsFormerFettFlatFooted-ESB.jpg|thumb|left|Jeihn was amongst the guardsmen who ambushed Sheckil.|250px]]
The Rebels were all later captured by Vader, who then changed elements of the deal concerning the prisoners with Calrissian.<ref name="ESB" /> This angered Calrissian, and caused him to secretly back out of the deal, deciding to help the Rebels instead.<ref name="ESB" /> Using the order "Code Force Seven,"<ref name="EGTC">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> he made Lobot aware of the change of plans, after which the aide gathered twelve guardsmen<ref name="ESBn">[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back'' novel]]</ref> including Jeihn, Selis, Spinoza, [[Pedar Solardo/Legends|Pedar Solardo]], [[Gir Endac]] and [[Razell Tameron]].<ref name="SWI" /> The group cut off a squad of six Imperials lead by [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Sheckil/Legends|Sheckil]], and accompanied by Calrissian, who were escorting three of the Rebel prisoners to Vader's [[ST 321/Legends|personal shuttle]]. The guards and Lobot drew their [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] on the outnumbered Imperials, who surrendered, allowing Calrissian to free the prisoners. The Baron Administrator then ordered that the Imperials be quietly taken to the [[Cloud City Security Tower]], which the Wing Guard used as a detention center, as to not raise suspicion in the other Imperials. After Jeihn and the other Guardsmen escorted the Imperials away, Calrissian and the other Rebels made their escape, although this left Cloud City under the control of the Empire.<ref name="ESB" />

==Personality and traits==
Corman Jeihn was a light skinned Human with [[Color/Legends|black]] hair.<ref name="ESB" /> He was not involved in the corruption that had swelled within the Wing Guards ranks under the Baron Administrator who served before Calrissian, [[Dominic Raynor]].<ref name="FB">{{Facebook|username=star-wars-sourcebooks|url=notes/star-wars-sourcebooks/naming-the-cloud-city-wing-guards/714850175231759|name=Star Wars Sourcebooks|date=2014-03-06}}</ref>

==Equipment==
Jeihn wore the standard blue uniform that all guardsmen wore while serving in the Wing Guard, and carried a standard issue [[Relby-k23 blaster pistol]].<ref name="ESB" />

==Behind the scenes==
Corman Jeihn first appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']] in which he was portrayed by an uncredited extra.<ref name="ESB" /> He was identified in [[2014]], when several of the Wing Guards were named in the [[Rogues Gallery (department)|''Rogues Gallery'']] feature of [[Star Wars Insider 148|''Star Wars Insider'' 148]]. The feature was written by [[Tim Veekhoven]], [[Kevin Beentjes]] and [[Sander de Lange]],<ref name="SWI" /> who later said in a Facebook post that all of the Wing Guards in the article who had not previously been established as corrupt were not corrupt, and most were "good guys" who opposed the corruption.<ref name="FB" />
